Anthropic has confirmed that it has a wet biology lab where it can use its AI models to run physical experiments.

AI leaders have been promising that AI is the key to curing human disease. Dario Amodei opined just last week: “I believe that AI could cure most major diseases in the next 5–10 years.” To do that, an LLM would have to have methods to test its theories in real life.

“We believe that to do biology, the final test is still, and will be for a while, in real lab work,” Anthropic’s head of life sciences, Eric Kauderer-Abrams told Reuters. “We absolutely are doing that today.” He added that the lab operates like most biotech labs: Anthropic conducts some research there while also working with externals partners.

This news probably shouldn’t be shocking. Anthropic bought Coefficient Bio, a stealth AI biotech, in April. It declined to say what the wet lab is working on, except that it’s not focused on drug discovery. Anthropic doesn’t want to give the appearance of competing with the pharma industry, where it has numerous major customers and partners. (For instance, it just announced a deal to work with Novo Nordisk on joint drug discovery.) Anthropic has already faced backlash for launching products perceived to compete with those of its customers.
To that end, Anthropic also launched a Life Sciences Verification Program this week, to give vetted bio researchers access to its most powerful models.

But the world is still reeling from the resignation of Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon, who warned that “the people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade.” Anthropic’s own alignment lead gave the odds at greater than 10% that AI could exterminate humanity within the next decade.

The fervor has grown so intense that CEO Dario Amodei published a post last weekend calling on the industry to slow down and institute self-regulation. He has repeatedly called bioterrorism one of AI’s biggest risks.

The juxtaposition of these dire warnings and the wet lab has not gone unnoticed in the tech industry. As investor and AI coding startup founder Chamath Palihapitiya posted on X, somewhat tongue-in-cheek: “The group behind such hits as: “We’re All Going To Die” and “Regulate Me Now” are building a wet lab in SF. I do not recommend this.”

Military aircraft were already in the air this spring when U.S. officials made an alarming discovery: the intelligence driving an armed operation against a Chinese vessel had been hallucinated by an AI chatbot. The operation was aborted at the last minute, narrowly averting a potential conflict with China, CNN reported on Friday.

The episode underscores a growing concern among military officials and outside experts: As decision-makers lean more heavily on AI, the errors these systems produce can travel up the chain of command before being questioned.
The intelligence report, which circulated during the war with Iran, said the vessel was carrying components for a nuclear weapons program.

The false intelligence originated with a Special Operations Command analyst who queried an AI chatbot to synthesize open-source data with classified signals intelligence. The chatbot misidentified the ship’s cargo manifest. The analyst then used the tool a second time to format the erroneous findings into an official-looking summary, which was circulated across command channels.

The near-miss comes as the U.S military races to integrate AI to accelerate decision-making and maintain its edge over China. The Pentagon has described AI as delivering a significant advantage in speeding up its kill chain so commanders can respond in the right time. But the same speed that makes AI attractive may also allow hallucinations with insufficient human oversight.

“It’s important for service members to understand the uncertainty inherent to LLMs,” said Jake Steckler, research scholar at GovAI and veteran U.S. Army officer in a written response to TechCrunch. “But it’s especially critical for any decisions that could lead to use of force, like targeting, intelligence analysis, or operational planning. There are life and death consequences for those decisions.”

Still, Steckler says, the incident should serve as a call to add more safeguards to AI, not a reason to avoid it. “These tools can be useful in the right contexts and with the right safeguards in place,” he said. “But prioritizing adoption speed over all else will likely lead to incidents that only make service members lose trust in these systems, which ultimately is only going to slow adoption.”

fulltext: IT之家 9 月 19 日消息，苹果设计团队在接受外媒《GQ》采访时，详细介绍了折叠屏手机 iPhone Duo 的设计理念、软件交互以及未来发展方向。本次参与采访者包括苹果 CEO John Ternus、工业设计副总裁 Molly Anderson 和人机界面设计副总裁 Steve Lemay。
Anderson 表示，苹果在设计 iPhone Duo 时参考了人们熟悉的纸质笔记本，目标是在提供更大显示空间的同时，让设备保持足够紧凑，方便用户随身携带：
iPhone Duo 的机身比例源自国际 A 系列纸张标准，使设备在折叠和展开状态下都能够保持相同的比例。人们都熟悉笔记本放在口袋里和随身携带时的感受，因此苹果希望借此解决’如何在提供更多空间的同时，保持设备紧凑’的问题。
Anderson 还介绍了 iPhone Duo 铰链阻尼的设计，该机铰链阻尼存在“可变扭矩曲线”，设备开启初期较为轻松，随着展开角度变化逐渐增加阻力，使屏幕开合时存在较佳手感，也更易促使用户在完全平整状态下使用设备。
在软件设计方面，Lemay 表示，苹果的核心思路是让用户感觉展开 iPhone Duo 就像是在扩展手中原本已经持有的设备。为此，苹果尽可能保持操作控件的位置和辨识度，让用户展开手机后无需重新寻找原本使用的按钮。同时，手机展开动画经过专门设计，使内屏看起来像是在外屏下方逐渐展开并延伸出来。
Lemay 强调，苹果从一开始就希望 iPhone Duo 成为一个完整统一的使用体验，而不是将两款不同产品简单拼接在一起。他还明确表示，Mac 是 iPhone Duo 交互设计的重要参考对象之一，同时苹果也借鉴了 iPad 和现有 iPhone 的设计理念，并将最终体验形容为这些产品设计元素的“精华集合”。
采访还谈到了苹果对 iPhone Duo 未来发展的预期。Lemay 认为，开发者可能会创造出许多苹果设计团队此前没有预料到的使用方式，其中部分创新甚至可能成为整个折叠屏行业的新方向，并反过来影响未来 iPhone Duo 产品的设计。

ChatGPT broke Diogo Almeida’s heart.

Almeida was an OpenAI researcher who helped build the chatbot and then invent reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), the model-training technique perhaps most responsible for our current age of AI. But despite its capabilities, he was disappointed.

“We have lightning in a bottle, and yet it is not useful,” Almeida told TechCrunch. “I’ve been battling that problem since then. It took me a while to come to the conclusion: The problem is we are optimizing for human language … We have been super good at human language for four years, but it’s not useful for automation because computers speak a different language.”

Two years ago, Almeida left OpenAI to start TypeSafe AI, a startup trying to fix that problem. This week, the company released a new transformer-based model, Jev, that is not a large language model (LLM). It doesn’t output text, but instead produces probabilities, or what the company calls “calibrated decisions.”

Eschewing language does a few things: It makes the model incredibly cheap and fast, and because users define the outputs in advance, it cannot hallucinate. Its output tokens are free, and input tokens are metered by the billion, not the million.

Developers are taking a great interest in the product; the company briefly lost the ability to serve users from its API because demand was so high. Jev appears most useful for software automation. Thus far, software developers see it as a cheaper and more robust way to incorporate intelligence into their code.

For example, Pranit Sharma, a software engineer at Vercel, a company making agentic infrastructure, said his company had used OpenAI’s ChatGPT Luna 5.6 to run a classifier to review commands for safety. When Vercel replaced OpenAI’s Luna with Jev, it got results five to 18 times more quickly and with greater accuracy.

Another developer, Bryo AI CTO Nikhil Mudholkar, tested Jev against Gemini for classifying business emails. In his test, Gemini was slightly more accurate, but 10 to 20 times more expensive. More interesting to Mudholkar were Jev’s confidence scores — “it is the only one that hands back a real probability which makes it ideal for automating workflows!!”

Besides replacing LLMs in certain use cases, the new model can also augment them, acting as a smart check on misbehavior. Using agents to monitor agents can quickly become expensive, but using Jev to do so, Almeida argues, makes sense. He sees users deploying Jev to track LLM agent traces and prevent jailbreaks.

“At the end of the day, it delegates the hallucination problem a little bit to the user,” explained Armin Ronacher, the CTO of Earendil, which builds the open source model harness Pi. “The user has to say, okay, if this only comes back with 50% probability, maybe this is a coin toss, and I disregard it. But if it’s 95%, sure, then I can do something with it.”

Another potential use for Jev is model routing, Ronacher said. Predicting whether a given workload requires a specific model would be useful, but using an LLM for the job would be expensive. Jev’s low cost and speed make that kind of real-time sorting possible.

And that’s Almeida’s hope. The model is named after William Stanley Jevons, the 19th-century economist whose eponymous paradox describes how the falling cost of a commodity can lead to it being used more and more. In this case, the falling cost of intelligence should lead to its widespread deployment.

“We think that there’s just going to be smart software all over the place in a way that’s emergent and distributed … much more like the early internet than you know like the mega apps that people are trying to build right now,” Almeida said.

Almeida is tight-lipped about the model’s architecture, which outside observers suspect is built on top of an open-weight LLM. The company refers to Jev as a “System One model,” focused on intuition rather than reasoning, and specifically focused on the right task. Almeida says Jev is trained exclusively on synthetic data using a technique he calls “reinforcement learning from calibrated decisions.”

“We made an early bet that we will be making all of our data, and that has been one of the best bets I’ve ever made in my life — better than our launch, in my opinion, better than RLHF,” he told TechCrunch. “Half of [our company] is a lab that basically owns this entire subfield of statistically well-understood synthetic data, and that is now my life joy.”
For now, Jev stands alone as this kind of model, but Ronacher expects that competitors will spring up now that its utility is apparent.
“We should have seen this earlier in many ways, but presumably because the LLMs are so cheap and subsidized, you often don’t have to be creative yet,” he said.

TypeSafe itself will be building more versions of the model, in new modalities. Asked if TypeSafe is a frontier lab, Almeida said, “the main product of frontier labs is fear or hype. I would like our main product to be intelligence…[but we are] not a lab in the sense of, you know, like bet on infinite wealth, or a religion, or building God in a data center, or whatever is the thing of today.”

ChatGPT伤了Diogo Almeida的心。
Almeida是一名OpenAI研究人员，他帮助构建了聊天机器人，然后从人类反馈中发明了强化学习（ RLHF ） ，这可能是我们当前人工智能时代最主要的模型训练技术。但尽管有这些能力，他还是很失望。
“我们的瓶子里有闪电，但它没有用，”阿尔梅达告诉TechCrunch。“从那时起，我一直在与这个问题作斗争。我花了一段时间才得出结论：问题是我们正在针对人类语言进行优化……我们已经擅长人类语言四年了，但由于计算机说不同的语言，这对自动化没有用。”
两年前， Almeida离开OpenAI ，创立了TypeSafe AI ，这是一家试图解决这个问题的初创公司。本周，该公司发布了一种新的基于变压器的模型Jev ，它不是大型语言模型（ LLM ）。它不输出文本，而是产生概率，或公司所谓的“校准决策”。
避开语言可以做一些事情：它使模型变得非常便宜和快速，并且由于用户预先定义了输出，因此它不会产生幻觉。其输出代币是免费的，输入代币的计量单位是十亿，而不是百万。
开发人员对该产品非常感兴趣；由于需求如此之高，该公司暂时失去了从其API为用户提供服务的能力。Jev似乎对软件自动化最有用。到目前为止，软件开发人员认为这是一种更便宜、更健壮的方式，可以将智能整合到他们的代码中。
例如，制造代理基础设施的公司Vercel的软件工程师Pranit Sharma表示，他的公司使用OpenAI的ChatGPT Luna 5.6运行分类器来审查安全命令。当Vercel用Jev取代OpenAI的Luna时，它以更快的速度和更高的准确性获得了5到18倍的结果。
另一位开发人员Bryo AI首席技术官Nikhil Mudholkar测试了Jev与Gemini对业务电子邮件的分类。在他的测试中，双子座的准确度略高，但价格高出10到20倍。对Mudholkar来说，更有趣的是Jev的信心得分-- “这是唯一一个返回真实概率的得分，这使其成为自动化工作流程的理想选择！ ！”
除了在某些用例中取代LLM之外，新模型还可以增强它们，对不当行为进行智能检查。Almeida认为，使用代理监控代理很快就会变得昂贵，但使用Jev这样做是有道理的。他看到用户部署Jev来跟踪LLM代理跟踪并防止越狱。
Earendil的首席技术官Armin Ronacher解释说： “最终，它会将幻觉问题委托给用户。「用户不得不说，好吧，如果这只有50%的概率回来，也许这是抛硬币，我无视它。但如果它是95% ，当然，那么我可以用它做点什么。”
Ronacher说， Jev的另一个潜在用途是模型路由。预测给定的工作负载是否需要特定的模型将是有用的，但使用LLM进行工作将是昂贵的。Jev的低成本和速度使这种实时分拣成为可能。
这就是阿尔梅达的希望。该模型以19世纪经济学家威廉·斯坦利·杰文斯（ William Stanley Jevons ）的名字命名，杰文斯的同名悖论描述了商品成本下降如何导致商品被越来越多地使用。在这种情况下，智能成本的下降应该会导致其广泛部署。
Almeida说： “我们认为，将会有智能软件以一种新兴和分布的方式遍布各地......更像是早期的互联网，而不是人们现在试图构建的大型应用程序。”
Almeida对该模型的架构守口如瓶，外部观察家怀疑该模型是建立在开放式法学硕士之上的。该公司将Jev称为“System One模型” ，专注于直觉而不是推理，并特别关注正确的任务。Almeida说， Jev专门使用一种他称之为“从校准决策中强化学习”的技术来训练合成数据。
他告诉TechCrunch ： “我们早些时候打赌，我们将制作所有数据，这是我一生中做过的最好的赌注之一—在我看来，比我们的推出更好，比RLHF更好。” “[我们公司]的一半是一个实验室，基本上拥有统计上易于理解的合成数据的整个子领域，这现在是我的生活乐趣。”
目前， Jev作为这种模式是独一无二的，但Ronacher预计，由于其效用显而易见，竞争对手将如雨后春笋般涌现。
他说： “我们应该在很多方面早点看到这一点，但大概是因为LLM是如此便宜和补贴，你通常不必有创造力。”
TypeSafe本身将以新的方式构建更多版本的模型。当被问及TypeSafe是否是一个前沿实验室时， Almeida说： “前沿实验室的主要产品是恐惧或炒作。我希望我们的主要产品是智能…… [但我们]不是一个实验室，就像押注无限的财富，或宗教，或在数据中心建立上帝，或今天的任何事情。”

Google is testing a new product designed to help families coordinate with the support of an AI agent. This week, the search giant introduced a new version of CC, an AI agent designed to work across email, calendar, chats, and tasks. With the update, CC now focuses on keeping families organized, planning for the day ahead, and even handling family-specific tasks, like signing permission slips, creating shopping lists, or crafting weekly meal plans.

The move to make CC more family-focused comes as a number of AI startups are experimenting with how to best fit agentic AI into consumers’ lives. Some AI tools, like Ollie and Fambot, for instance, have aimed their services directly at helping parents and families.

Google’s CC, meanwhile, began its life as a productivity agent that connected to Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive, and the wider web to understand your day, then deliver a “Your Day Ahead” briefing to your inbox. In May, the tool came to the Gemini app as “Daily Brief.”

Google said user requests showed that people wanted to use the feature more for household management tasks. They wanted AI to help them keep up with kids’ school schedules, sports practices, bills, meal plans, and more.
As a result, Google shifted CC to become an agent for families that helps run their households.

Now, CC is getting its own Google account, so it can collaborate with family members on tasks, while also maintaining its own specific set of permissions for accessing data. Google explains that each family member chooses what they want to share — like emails about school events, sports, clubs, birthday party invites, doctor appointments, or anything else. These can be forwarded to CC via its email address, or shared automatically.

To automate sharing, users can pick the email senders whose messages they always want to share with CC going forward, like schools, travel companies, clubs, or sports teams. (CC will also suggest email senders to add on a weekly basis.)
The company says CC currently supports up to six family members who can share information and collaborate with the agent.

Beyond email, CC can also coordinate household activities by tracking important dates and to-dos, and then automatically adding them to the calendar or a shared task list. That means, for instance, every time the orthodontist sends an email confirmation of your next appointment or the school announces a teacher workday, CC can put it on the shared calendar.

What’s more, the agent can manage select tasks on a family’s behalf, like filling out permission slips or activity registration PDFs, making school supply shopping lists, planning weekly meals, figuring out drive times between activities, creating shared Docs or Sheets, and more. It will even ask for missing details, as needed, and update its group memory so it can be more helpful going forward.

Google notes that CC runs on its own isolated cloud computer, powered by Gemini and Google’s agentic harness, Antigravity. The experiment is only available for U.S. users with a personal Gmail account, who are ages 18 and up.

That’s a big drawback for the time being because it means older kids, like tweens and teens, can’t use the service unless they lie about their age on their Google accounts. It also means they can’t use it with their school-provided emails, despite the fact that many attend schools that run everything on Chromebooks and Google apps and have inboxes filled with school-related updates.

CC could help larger households, where parents have to coordinate with each other and with other adults, like grandparents, caregivers, nannies, or adult children still living at home, which tends to be more common these days.
Existing CC users will be invited via email in the coming days to upgrade their accounts, Google says, while new users can join a waitlist to access the AI agent.

谷歌正在测试一款新产品，旨在帮助家庭在人工智能代理的支持下进行协调。本周，这家搜索巨头推出了新版本的CC ，这是一种旨在跨电子邮件、日历、聊天和任务工作的人工智能代理。通过此次更新， CC现在专注于保持家庭秩序、提前一天进行规划，甚至处理家庭特定的任务，例如签署许可单、创建购物清单或制定每周膳食计划。
此举使CC更加以家庭为中心，因为许多人工智能初创公司正在尝试如何将代理人工智能最好地融入消费者的生活。例如，一些人工智能工具，如Ollie和Fambot ，将他们的服务直接用于帮助父母和家庭。
与此同时，谷歌的CC最初是一个生产力代理，与Gmail、Google日历、Google云端硬盘和更广泛的网络连接，以了解您的一天，然后向您的收件箱发送“您的一天”简报。5月，该工具作为“每日简报”出现在Gemini应用程序中。
谷歌表示，用户的请求表明，人们希望更多地将该功能用于家庭管理任务。他们希望人工智能帮助他们跟上孩子们的上学时间表、体育活动、账单、膳食计划等。
因此，谷歌将CC转变为帮助家庭经营家庭的代理商。
现在， CC正在获得自己的Google帐户，因此它可以与家人在任务上进行协作，同时还保留了自己访问数据的特定权限集。Google解释说，每个家庭成员都可以选择自己想要分享的内容，例如有关学校活动、体育、俱乐部、生日派对邀请、医生预约或其他任何内容的电子邮件。这些信息可以通过其电子邮件地址转发给抄送，也可以自动共享。
为了自动共享，用户可以选择一直希望与CC共享消息的电子邮件发件人，例如学校、旅游公司、俱乐部或运动队。（抄送还将建议电子邮件发件人每周添加。）
该公司表示， CC目前最多支持六名家庭成员，他们可以与代理共享信息和进行协作。
除了电子邮件， CC还可以跟踪重要的日期和待办事项，然后自动将其添加到日历或共享任务列表中，从而协调家庭活动。这意味着，例如，每次正畸医生发送电子邮件确认您的下一次预约或学校宣布教师工作日， CC都可以将其放在共享日历上。
此外，客服代表还可以代表家人管理特定任务，例如填写许可单或活动登记PDF文件、制作学校用品购物清单、规划每周餐点、计算活动之间的驾驶时间、创建共享文档或表格等。它甚至会根据需要询问缺失的详细信息，并更新其小组记忆，以便在未来更有帮助。
谷歌指出， CC在自己的隔离云计算机上运行，由Gemini和谷歌的代理线束Antigravity提供支持。该实验仅适用于拥有个人Gmail账号且年满18周岁的美国用户。
目前这是一个很大的缺点，因为这意味着年龄较大的孩子，如青少年，除非他们在Google帐户上谎报年龄，否则无法使用该服务。这也意味着他们不能在学校提供的电子邮件中使用它，尽管许多学校在Chromebook和Google应用程序上运行所有内容，并且收件箱中装满了与学校相关的更新。
CC可以帮助较大的家庭，在这些家庭中，父母必须相互协调，并与其他成年人（如祖父母、照顾者、保姆或仍住在家中的成年子女）协调，这在当今往往更为常见。
谷歌表示，未来几天将通过电子邮件邀请现有的CC用户升级其帐户，而新用户可以加入等待名单以访问AI代理。

fulltext: 协同布局AI基础设施

9月17日，上海无问芯穹智能科技股份有限公司（以下简称“无问芯穹”）与北京华环电子股份有限公司（以下简称“华环电子”）签署战略合作框架协议。双方将结合各自产业与技术优势，围绕AI基础设施创新与产业应用深化合作，共同探索算力与网络协同发展新模式。此次签约标志着双方在AI基础设施领域的协同进入新阶段，将推动计算、网络与AI原生基础设施深度融合，为人工智能规模化应用提供更加高效、稳定和开放的基础设施支撑。
华环电子党总支书记、董事长郭萌，无问芯穹上海总经理曾书霖代表签约；
清控集团党委书记、董事长甄佳，清华大学电子工程系长聘教授、IEEE Fellow汪玉，无问芯穹CTO李伯勋见证签约。
优势互补，协同布局AI基础设施

随着大模型和智能体应用加速发展，AI基础设施正从单一算力资源为中心，转向计算、网络、软件平台与模型服务的系统协同。华环电子是国家级专精特新重点“小巨人”企业，与清华大学电子工程系、清华科技产业体系有着深厚的历史渊源。华环电子深耕信息通信与光网络领域30余年，光传输设备长期服务中国移动、中国电信、中国联通三大运营商，并广泛应用于电力、交通等行业专用通信网络。无问芯穹同样源自清华电子系，作为领先的AI原生基础设施服务商，依托多元异构、软硬协同、自主式AI等核心技术，构建Agentic Infra自主式基础设施平台与Agentic MaaS大模型服务平台，已服务千余家AI企业与科研机构。
根据协议，无问芯穹将发挥异构算力管理与AI软件平台优势，华环电子将发挥网络通信、硬件研发和工程实施运维能力，双方将共同探索面向国产异构算力的基础设施协同方案，形成从算力调度到网络传输、从软件平台到硬件工程的端到端能力互补。
联合探索智算中心解决方案

在智算中心解决方案方面，双方拟联合推进方案设计、软硬件适配、集成交付与运行维护等环节。无问芯穹已打造面向异构集群的大模型跨域训练系统，通过计算通信重叠的流水编排、自适应通信流调度和异构算力调度机制，系统性破解算力聚合难题；该系统已在全国部署触达超37,000P算力、覆盖16种主流芯片。华环电子将在光传输与网络接入领域提供高速互联与稳定传输支撑。双方还将建立常态化合作机制，持续开展技术验证与成果转化。
探索“Token工厂”新模式
双方计划进一步探索以Token为标准化产出、以AI应用需求为牵引的基础设施供给新模式，聚焦“国产大模型+国产芯片”优化闭环。无问芯穹Agentic MaaS大模型服务平台致力于Token规模化、高质量生产，过去一年已推动推理成本下降10倍。华环电子的硬件研发、网络通信与工程运维能力，将为Token工厂从建设到运营提供工程化支撑。

fulltext: IT之家 9 月 18 日消息，日前，21 世纪经济报道援引产业链人士消息称，特斯拉相关团队已于 9 月 16 日落地宁波，并于 17 日开启新一轮针对旗下机器人业务的量产审厂。据称此轮审厂将实质导向机器人 Optimus 的量产，已向供应链企业下达相关订单。
按计划，特斯拉今年将下线约 5 万台 Optimus 机器人，在世界各地特斯拉超级工厂中部署。不过，现阶段普通消费者仍无购买渠道。
消息称特斯拉去年 9 月在华曾启动一轮机器人审厂工作，涉及的公司包括拓普集团、三花智控、浙江荣泰、新泉股份、均胜电子等传统特斯拉汽车供应链企业。若此轮审厂属实，意味着特斯拉正将更多汽车供应链资源导入机器人业务，为其规模化生产做准备。
9 月 18 日，特斯拉方面未对相关情况作出回应。第一财经以投资者身份致电总部位于宁波的拓普集团、均胜电子等公司，询问相关进展。
拓普集团工作人员回复称，暂时没有接到特斯拉团队审厂的相关通知。该工作人员介绍，特斯拉相关研发人员平时就在宁波的工厂，研发人员既有来自汽车业务的，也有机器人业务的。双方就直线和旋转执行器、灵巧手执行器等方面有进行合作，机器人部件基地已经准备就绪。
报道认为，这一回应显示，拓普集团与特斯拉在机器人执行器领域的合作早已存在，相关产能也处于待命状态。
作为特斯拉汽车供应链企业的均胜电子工作人员表示，因有保密性要求，涉及下游客户的情况不方便回应。均胜电子的态度较为谨慎，未对审厂消息给出正面确认。
三花智控工作人员则回复称，不清楚特斯拉新一轮审厂的情况。他提到，公司有在配合大客户进行机器人关节执行器的开发。报道指出，这一表述与拓普集团的回应相呼应，同样指向供应链企业已在机器人关节部件上展开实质性配合。
据IT之家此前报道，特斯拉 CEO 埃隆 · 马斯克 7 月曾坦言，Optimus 的生产一开始会极其缓慢，因为一切都是全新的，与造车不同。
马斯克在今年 3 月谈到 Optimus 3 机器人时，将其描述为“迄今为止全球最先进的机器人”，并表示：“我还没见过任何能媲美 Optimus 3 的机器人演示。”在产能规划上，马斯克表示，低产量生产可在夏季启动，高产量生产则会在 2027 年展开。

cards.summary: 【GitHub】Hot takes turn complicated topics into one confident sentence. That makes them great for engagement, but not necessarily for understanding. At the surface level, they do not matter much. You agree, di…
fulltext: Hot takes turn complicated topics into one confident sentence. That makes them great for engagement, but not necessarily for understanding.
At the surface level, they do not matter much. You agree, disagree, repost, argue for a few minutes, and move on. Sometimes the take is directionally right. Sometimes it is complete nonsense.

The value of hot takes is in what happens when you stop reacting and start pulling them apart. Under what conditions is this true? What context is missing? What assumptions does it make? What changes when you apply it to real work?
That is where the depth is. A good hot take gives you something sharp enough to question. The questions are where you find the useful ideas.
We explore all this and more in the latest episode of the GitHub Podcast!
Not ready to dive in yet? Here are a few of the common AI hot takes we discussed and what we can get from them.
Yes, you do. You are still responsible for the code.
But that does not mean every generated line needs the same level of attention.

A production authentication refactor deserves a different review process than a CSS experiment. A codebase you have maintained for 10 years steers your instincts differently than one you opened this morning. Pretending every change carries the same risk is not rigor. It is just a bad use of time.
A simple rule: review until you can explain and own the outcome.

Sometimes that work starts before the agent writes anything. You read the current implementation, map the dependencies, identify edge cases, and make a plan. By the time the first implementation exists, you already understand what it should do and where it could go wrong.
Other times, the generated code itself needs most of your attention. You inspect the error handling, permissions, data access, performance, accessibility, and tests.
AI moves the effort around. It does not make the work disappear.
The actual skill is knowing where the risk lives.
The reality is a little more nuanced. More teams are asking candidates how they use AI. That makes sense. These tools are becoming part of software development.
But no one thinks every developer needs the same workflow, the same tools, or the same level of enthusiasm.
The stronger signal is judgment.

Can you explain when you use AI and when you work manually? Can you describe how you review generated code? Can you talk honestly about speed, quality, security, and maintainability? Can you change your process as the tools change?

If a company is building AI products or uses AI heavily in its engineering workflow, refusing to touch AI may make you a bad fit. That is not controversial. But total dependence and total refusal are rarely good answers.
The better answer is a clear explanation of how you work, what you trust the tools to do, and where you keep yourself in the loop.
That kind of fluency is becoming part of the craft.
No. They solve different problems.

The Model Context Protocol gives agents a standard way to connect to tools and data. That standard matters when you want systems to work together reliably. Agents need structured ways to call tools, fetch context, and take action.

Skills are closer to packaged expertise. A skill can explain how a team works, how a project should be changed, how a tool should be used, or which conventions matter. Since skills are often written in Markdown, people can read them too. That readability is part of their value.
MCP can provide access. Skills can explain how to use that access well.
You do not need to pick a winner. Use standards for shared interfaces. Use skills for context, process, and best practices.
The combination is much more interesting than the argument.
RAG is not dead. It is just not the newest thing people want to post about.

Retrieval-augmented generation gives an AI system relevant information outside the model’s training data. That can include documentation, support history, product details, internal knowledge, or codebase context.
Without good retrieval, the model has to rely on what it already knows or spend extra time searching for context. That wastes tokens, slows down the work, and makes incomplete answers more likely.
Good retrieval helps the model start closer to the answer. It narrows the search space and grounds the response in information that actually matters.

Agents, skills, MCP, and RAG can all exist in the same workflow. An agent might use MCP to access a tool, follow a skill for project-specific instructions, and use retrieval to find the right supporting context.
These things are not fighting each other. Treating them like they are misses how people actually build with AI.

There are valid reasons to fine-tune a model. Still, modern models have seen a huge number of common frameworks, patterns, naming conventions, and architectures. If a model cannot make sense of your codebase, there is a decent chance a new teammate will struggle too.
AI is becoming another pressure test for maintainability, alongside code review, testing, onboarding, and the poor person debugging this six months from now.
Clear structure helps. Consistent naming helps. Readable tests, useful abstractions, and current documentation help.
Those things make a codebase easier for an agent to understand, but more importantly, they make it easier for a person to review, debug, and extend.
AI-assisted development rewards codebases that make their intent obvious.
That is a good thing.
AI will keep producing strong opinions because the tools are changing quickly, and we are all still figuring out our workflows.
You do not need to pick a permanent side in every debate.
The better response to an interesting take is not another take. Test the idea. Build something. Document what happened. Give everyone something real to learn from.

Pollinations AI is doing that by experimenting with a generative AI platform where contributors can earn credits, called pollen, by improving the project. People can open and solve issues, contribute models, and complete quests. The project raises real questions about incentives, quality, scale, and what open source contribution could look like when AI lowers the barrier to participation.

Avian Visitors is doing it in a completely different way. It is a build log for a bird-listening e-ink display that turns birds visiting an apartment balcony into changing wall art. It combines a microphone, Raspberry Pi, e-ink screen, 3D-printed parts, generated bird images, and thoughtful documentation.
These projects do not settle every AI debate. They do something more useful: they create evidence, expose tradeoffs, and give other people a place to start.

Read enough code to own the result. Build enough AI fluency to explain how you work. Use MCP when a standard interface helps. Use skills when context and process matter. Keep RAG when grounded information makes the system better. If your code confuses both people and models, treat that as a maintainability problem.
Most importantly, do something with what you learn.

fulltext_cn: HOT把复杂的话题变成一个自信的句子。这使他们非常适合参与，但不一定适合理解。
从表面上看，它们并不重要。您同意、不同意、重新发布、争论几分钟，然后继续前进。有时采取的方向是正确的。有时这完全是胡说八道。
热拍的价值在于当你停止反应并开始将它们分开时会发生什么。这在什么情况下是真的？缺少什么背景？它做出了什么假设？当您将其应用于实际工作时，会发生什么变化？
这就是深度所在。一个好的热拍会给你一些足够尖锐的东西来质疑。问题是您找到有用想法的地方。
我们在最新一期的GitHub播客中探讨了所有这些以及更多内容！
还没准备好潜水吗？以下是我们讨论的一些常见的人工智能热门话题，以及我们可以从中获得什么。
是的，您有。您仍需对代码负责。
但这并不意味着每条生成的线路都需要相同的关注度。
生产身份验证重构应采用与CSS实验不同的审核流程。您维护了10年的代码库与您今天早上打开的代码库的本能不同。假装每次变革都具有相同的风险并不严格。这只是对时间的不良利用。
一个简单的规则：查看，直到您可以解释并拥有结果。
有时，在客服代表写下任何内容之前，工作就开始了。您阅读当前实现，映射依赖关系，识别边缘案例并制定计划。到第一次实现时，您已经了解了它应该做什么以及它可能会出错的地方。
其他时候，生成的代码本身就需要您的大部分注意力。您检查错误处理、权限、数据访问、性能、可访问性和测试。
人工智能将精力转移到周围。它不会使作品消失。
实际的技能是知道风险在哪里。
现实有点微妙。越来越多的团队询问求职者他们如何使用人工智能。这是有道理的。这些工具正在成为软件开发的一部分。
但没有人认为每个开发人员都需要相同的工作流程、相同的工具或相同的热情。
更强的信号是判断。
您能解释一下您何时使用人工智能以及何时手动工作吗？您能描述一下您是如何查看生成的代码的吗？您能诚实地谈论速度、质量、安全性和可维护性吗？您能否随着工具的变化而改变您的流程？
如果一家公司正在构建人工智能产品或在其工程工作流程中大量使用人工智能，拒绝触摸人工智能可能会使您不合适。这没有争议。但完全依赖和完全拒绝很少是好的答案。
更好的答案是清楚地解释你的工作方式，你信任的工具，以及你让自己保持在循环中的位置。
这种流畅性正在成为工艺的一部分。
不，他们解决了不同的问题。
模型上下文协议为代理提供了连接到工具和数据的标准方式。当您希望系统可靠地协同工作时，这一标准很重要。客服代表需要系统化的方式来调用工具、获取背景信息并采取行动。
技能更接近打包的专业知识。技能可以解释团队如何工作、项目应如何更改、工具应如何使用或哪些约定很重要。由于技能通常用Markdown编写，因此人们也可以阅读它们。这种可读性是其价值的一部分。
MCP可以提供访问权限。技能可以解释如何很好地利用这种访问权限。
您无需选择获胜者。使用共享接口的标准。将技能用于情境、流程和最佳实践。
这种组合比论点更有趣。
抹布没有死。这不是人们想要发布的最新内容。
检索增强生成为AI系统提供模型训练数据之外的相关信息。这可能包括文档、支持历史记录、产品详细信息、内部知识或代码库上下文。
如果没有良好的检索，模型必须依赖于它已经知道的内容，或者花费额外的时间搜索上下文。这会浪费代币，减慢工作速度，并使不完整的答案更有可能。
良好的检索有助于模型更接近答案。它缩小了搜索空间，并在实际重要的信息中为响应奠定了基础。
客服代表、技能、MCP和RAG都可以存在于同一个工作流程中。客服代表可能会使用MCP访问工具，遵循特定项目的技能说明，并使用检索查找正确的支持上下文。
这些东西不是在互相争斗。像对待他们一样对待他们，错过了人们如何使用人工智能进行实际构建。
微调模型是有正当理由的。尽管如此，现代模型已经出现了大量的通用框架、模式、命名约定和架构。如果模型无法理解您的代码库，那么新队友也很有可能会遇到困难。
人工智能正在成为可维护性的另一个压力测试，以及代码审查、测试、入职和六个月后调试的穷人。
清晰的结构有助于。一致的命名有助于。可读测试、有用的抽象和当前文档帮助。
这些东西使代理更容易理解代码库，但更重要的是，它们使人员更容易查看、调试和扩展。
人工智能辅助开发奖励代码库，使其意图显而易见。
這是 一件 好事 .
人工智能将继续产生强有力的意见，因为工具正在迅速变化，我们仍在研究我们的工作流程。
您无需在每次辩论中选择永久一方。
对有趣的拍摄做出更好的反应不是另一种拍摄。测试这个想法。建立一些东西。记录发生了什么。给每个人一些真实的东西来学习。
